The counterexample $f=\mathbf 1_{\{x_1=0\}}$, $g=\mathbf 1_{\{x_1=1\}}$ gives $\langle f,T_\rho g\rangle=(1-\rho)/4$ and $\|f*g\|_2^2=1/8$, so $c_{\rho,n}\le 2(1-\rho)$ for every $n\ge1$. Solution 1 (constant 1), Solution 2 ($\rho-1/2$), and Solution 3 ($\rho$) all exceed $2(1-\rho)$ for $\rho$ near 1, so none can be the optimal constant.
